text:
Zeev Buium is 20, and Vancouver is leaning on him. He has played more than 24 minutes in three of his last four games and averages 21:21 on the season, a heavy load for a second-year defenseman on a team that has lost almost every game since late October.

The results are what you would expect from that combination: 4 assists, no goals, and the Canucks with 37.4% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. Pass it to Bulis's Daniel Wagner called one sequence against Philadelphia "appallingly bad gap control". Evolving-Hockey's read on his first season was similar, with chances against climbing when he played, but also partners in the bottom 7% by impact and +2.2 goals from drawing more penalties than he takes.

The reason for patience is the puck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying it in on 46% of his entries, and 28% of his shots came off the rush, well above a typical defenseman. Of 64 defensemen drafted around his slot with four-plus seasons, the median first full year was 0.24 points a game. He is at 0.20.
headline: Zeev Buium is playing big minutes on a losing team
